title: The Gilded Ember
premise: Odile Brightwater, a bone-carver whose carvings let him hear the dead, has hidden his gift for twelve years in the magic-outlawed city of Vell. When a dying courier presses a bone map into his hands, Odile learns the king has been hollowed out and replaced by a devouring spirit called the Gilded Ember, sustained by the stolen voices of every silenced mage. Pursued by the Ember's inquisitors, Odile gathers a found family of outcasts and follows the map to the king's buried heart, where he must choose between destroying the Ember and freeing the voices—including his mother's—trapped inside it. In the end, Odile gives up his own gift to unbind the king, discovering that his true identity was never the hearing, but the courage to speak.
about_author: Gideon Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing funerary carvings in coastal cathedral crypts before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy about quiet people with loud ghosts, and lives near the sea with an unrepentant cat.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Bones
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In the market of Vell, Odile sells harmless charms while secretly carving messages from the dead into bone trinkets. A bleeding courier collapses at his stall and forces the bone map into his hands, whispering that the king is already gone before dying. When inquisitors arrive asking questions, Odile realizes his invisibility has shattered. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant responsibility as safety becomes impossible.

chapters.title: A Company of the Unwanted
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, with interludes from the Ember wearing the king. Fleeing Vell, Odile assembles allies: Sera, a disgraced inquisitor seeking truth; Bramble, a child thief who can walk through wards; and Old Tamsin, the last hedge-witch. The map reveals the Ember feeds on imprisoned mage-voices beneath the palace. Emotional beat: tentative trust hardening into found family as each shares what they lost to the outlawry.

chapters.title: The Hollow Crown
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Infiltrating the palace through Bramble's stolen routes, the group reaches the vault of voices, where Odile hears his mother among the trapped dead. The Ember offers him a bargain: his gift and silence in exchange for his friends' lives. Sera is captured; Bramble is nearly consumed. Odile refuses and the vault erupts. Emotional beat: betrayal of self-preservation; loyalty chosen over survival at terrible cost.

chapters.title: What the Ember Leaves
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In the throne room, Odile carves his final piece—the king's own name, long erased—into the crown itself, giving the hollowed king a thread of self to seize. The Ember, starved of obedience, unravels as Odile surrenders his hearing to release the voices. The freed king outlawry is repealed; Odile, giftless but whole, opens a shop where the living finally speak to him. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; identity found in what remains.
